mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a three-month window signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household wealth and lower equity demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer and business confidence, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M MA and INDPRO YoY change < -3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based demand collapse, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 MoM change < -1% AND HOUST MoM change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle that boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) volatility above their 12-month averages signals labor market instability, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE volatility > 12M avg AND PAYEMS volatility > 12M avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of co-triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the real savings rate (proxied by RSAFS/GDPC1) above 8% for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary saving and lower marginal propensity to consume, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio > 0.08 for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.
